body_html:
Good night messages in Spanish range from a quick ¡buenas noches! to tender lines that close the day with someone you love. Spanish has a few beautiful phrases for this moment, like que descanses (rest well) and que sueñes con los angelitos (dream with the little angels), that English doesn’t quite match. Below are forty good night messages, grouped by who you are writing to, with translations and notes on tone.

Quick answer
  • Basic: ¡Buenas noches!
  • Warm: Que descanses. Que duermas bien.
  • Sweet: Sueña bonito, mi amor.
  • For kids: Que sueñes con los angelitos.
{{toc}}

Short good night messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Buenas noches!
    Good night!
  2. Que descanses.
    Rest well.
  3. Que duermas bien.
    Sleep well.
  4. Dulces sueños.
    Sweet dreams.
  5. Hasta mañana.
    See you tomorrow.
  6. Buenas noches, que mañana será un gran día.
    Good night, tomorrow will be a great day.
  7. A dormir, que mañana hay que madrugar.
    Off to bed, we have to get up early tomorrow.

Que descanses is probably the most common way to end a conversation at night in Mexico. It works with anyone, from your partner to a coworker.

For your partner

  1. Buenas noches, mi amor. Sueña bonito.
    Good night, my love. Sweet dreams.
  2. Ojalá estuvieras aquí para darte un beso de buenas noches.
    I wish you were here so I could kiss you good night.
  3. Me voy a dormir pensando en ti.
    I’m going to sleep thinking about you.
  4. Gracias por hacer de hoy un día especial. Te quiero.
    Thank you for making today special. I love you.
  5. Buenas noches, corazón. Mañana te veo.
    Good night, sweetheart. See you tomorrow.
  6. Que sueñes conmigo.
    Dream of me.
  7. Eres lo último en que pienso antes de dormir.
    You’re the last thing I think about before I fall asleep.
  8. Descansa, mi vida. Mañana es otro día para estar juntos.
    Rest, my love. Tomorrow is another day to be together.

For the difference between te quiero and te amo in messages like these, see {{link:te-quiero-vs-te-amo|te quiero vs te amo}}.

{{image:2}}

For children

  1. Buenas noches, mi amor. Que sueñes con los angelitos.
    Good night, sweetheart. Sweet dreams. (literally: dream with the little angels)
  2. A la cama, mi niño. Te quiero hasta la luna.
    Off to bed, my boy. I love you to the moon.
  3. Que descanses, princesa.
    Rest well, princess.
  4. Mañana jugamos más. Ahora, a dormir.
    We’ll play more tomorrow. Now, sleep.
  5. Duérmete ya, que mañana hay escuela.
    Go to sleep now, there’s school tomorrow.

For more bedtime phrases, see {{link:talking-to-kids-in-spanish|talking to kids in Spanish}}.

For family and friends

  1. Buenas noches, mamá. Que descanse.
    Good night, Mom. Rest well. (formal)
  2. Buenas noches a todos. Que Dios los bendiga.
    Good night, everyone. God bless you all.
  3. Gracias por la cena, la pasé muy bien. ¡Buenas noches!
    Thanks for dinner, I had a great time. Good night!
  4. Buenas noches, amiga. Mañana me cuentas todo.
    Good night, my friend. Tell me everything tomorrow.
  5. Llegué bien a casa. ¡Buenas noches!
    I got home safely. Good night!
  6. Descansa, que te lo mereces.
    Get some rest, you deserve it.

Llegué bien (I got home safely) is an important message in many families and friend groups, especially after a night out. Sending it is considered thoughtful.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Funny good night messages

  1. Me voy a dormir antes de que mi cama me reclame.
    I’m going to bed before my bed files a complaint.
  2. Buenas noches. Mañana, más café.
    Good night. Tomorrow, more coffee.
  3. Me despido, que mis ojos ya renunciaron.
    I’m signing off, my eyes have already quit.
  4. Hasta mañana, si el despertador lo permite.
    See you tomorrow, if the alarm clock allows it.

How to reply to a good night message

When someone sends you buenas noches, a short reply keeps it warm: Igualmente, que descanses (Same to you, rest well), Tú también, hasta mañana (You too, see you tomorrow) or, with a partner, Y tú sueña conmigo (And you dream of me). In family chats, Buenas noches, que Dios te bendiga is often answered with Amén, igualmente. If you are going to bed first, Ya me voy a dormir, platicamos mañana (I’m going to sleep, let’s talk tomorrow) is a natural way to end the conversation in Mexico; in Spain, hablamos mañana is more common.

{{image:3}}

Messages for hard days

  1. Sé que hoy fue difícil. Descansa, mañana será mejor.
    I know today was hard. Rest, tomorrow will be better.
  2. Aquí estoy si me necesitas. Buenas noches.
    I’m here if you need me. Good night.
  3. Mañana es un nuevo comienzo.
    Tomorrow is a fresh start.
  4. Que descanses y que todo salga bien mañana.
    Rest well and I hope everything goes well tomorrow.

For more words of support, see {{link:how-to-comfort-someone-in-spanish|how to comfort someone in Spanish}}.

Tips and common mistakes

  • Buena noche. The standard greeting is plural: buenas noches.
  • Que descansas. Wishes take the subjunctive: que descanses. See {{link:indicative-vs-subjunctive|indicative vs subjunctive}}.
  • Buenas noches as a greeting. It also means “good evening” when you arrive somewhere after dark.
  • Sueña con los angelitos for adults. It is sweet for kids; with adults it can sound playful or teasing.

In the morning, try {{link:good-morning-messages-in-spanish|good morning messages in Spanish}}. The RAE dictionary entry for descansar shows its everyday uses.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Good night messages in Spanish are a small habit with a big effect. Learn que descanses and sueña bonito, save a few favorites for the people you love, and end each day in Spanish. For more ready-to-send messages, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say good night in Spanish?
faq.a: Buenas noches. To wish someone a good rest, add que descanses or que duermas bien.

faq.q: What does “que sueñes con los angelitos” mean?
faq.a: Literally “may you dream with the little angels”. It is a sweet bedtime phrase, mostly for children.

faq.q: How do you say sweet dreams in Spanish?
Why is it “que descanses” and not “que descansas”?
faq.a: Because it is a wish, and wishes take the subjunctive.
